verify_method: Ported (Phase 0) then verified live via Exa + enriched via Consensus (2026-07-03). MH-01/02/03 confirmed against primary sources; MH-05 refreshed from stale 2013 stat to current NSCH figure. MH-04 and MH-06 remain PULL (not attempted this pass).

claims.claim: About one in four Nebraskans experiences a behavioral health issue each year, yet provider shortages and long wait times leave many unable to access care.
claims.source: BHECN (Behavioral Health Education Center of Nebraska), UNMC — 2026 Behavioral Health Workforce Capacity Report; UNMC Newsroom (Nov 7, 2025).
claims.expiry: BHECN publishes annually; refresh from unmc.edu/bhecn.

claims.claim: Nebraska's licensed behavioral health workforce grew 49% from 2010 to 2024 (2,279 to 3,397 providers), including a 24% increase in rural counties — yet demand continues to outpace supply, and Nebraska remains the only state that tracks its behavioral health workforce longitudinally.
claims.source: BHECN, The Licensed Behavioral Health Workforce in Nebraska: 2010 to 2024; 2026 Behavioral Health Workforce Capacity Report (released May 2026).
claims.expiry: Refresh with the next annual BHECN capacity report.
red_team_flags: Workforce growth (49%) and persistent shortage are not contradictory — pair them so a reviewer reads 'growing but still insufficient,' not a self-cancelling stat. Several Nebraska regions still require a 1+ hour drive to in-person behavioral health care.

claims.claim: Nationally in 2023, 39.7% of high school students experienced persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness, 20.4% seriously considered attempting suicide, and 9.5% attempted suicide.
claims.source: CDC, Youth Risk Behavior Survey, United States, 2023 (MMWR Supplement 73(4), Oct 2024).
claims.expiry: YRBS runs on a 2-year cycle; refresh with the 2025 YRBS (~2026 release).
red_team_flags: Exact figures confirmed against the CDC MMWR primary (also 28.5% reported poor mental health). Female and LGBQ+ students show markedly higher prevalence — segment if the funder's focus warrants.

claims.claim: Nebraska-specific youth behavioral-health figures (state-weighted YRBS or NRPFSS, including Douglas/Sarpy county coverage).
claims.source: NE DHHS YRBS results portal; fallback: Nebraska Risk and Protective Factor Student Survey (NRPFSS).
red_team_flags: Nebraska's YRBS participation/weighting varies by cycle — confirm whether 2023 state-weighted data exist before citing. NRPFSS has stronger county-level (Douglas/Sarpy) coverage.

claims.claim: About half (49.4%) of the estimated 7.7 million U.S. children with a treatable mental health disorder do not receive needed treatment from a mental health professional.
claims.source: Whitney, D.G. & Peterson, M.D. (2019). US National and State-Level Prevalence of Mental Health Disorders and Disparities of Mental Health Care Use in Children. JAMA Pediatrics, 173(4), 389-391 (2016 National Survey of Children's Health).
claims.expiry: REFRESHED from the stale CDC 2013 '20%' stat. Watch for a newer NSCH (2020+) treatment-gap analysis and update when available.
red_team_flags: This REPLACES the corpus's original 2013 '~20% identified and receive services' figure, which a knowledgeable federal reviewer would flag as outdated. The 49.4% untreated figure is the current, correctly framed statistic. State-level range: 29.5% (DC) to 72.2% (North Carolina).

efficacy_evidence.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy for children and adolescents
efficacy_evidence.cite: Thielemann et al., 2022, Child Abuse & Neglect (61 studies, 4,523 participants)
efficacy_evidence.finding: TF-CBT produced large improvements in post-traumatic stress (g=1.14) and was superior to control conditions — supporting it as a first-line treatment for traumatized children.

efficacy_evidence.title: Efficacy and moderators of CBT with a trauma focus in children and adolescents: an individual participant data meta-analysis
efficacy_evidence.cite: de Haan et al., 2023, The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health
efficacy_evidence.finding: IPD meta-analysis supports trauma-focused CBT as first-line treatment irrespective of age, gender, or trauma type, with the greatest benefit for the most distressed children.

claims.claim: HRSA Mental Health Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designations across the 16 southwest Iowa counties Project Harmony serves.
red_team_flags: Most SW Iowa counties carry whole-county MH HPSA designations; county-by-county designation IDs strengthen HRSA and rural proposals. Pull the current designation IDs.
